nodes.label: Unmet needs ranked by evidence strength (Phase 3 capstone)
nodes.rationale: 11 needs ranked; H1 and H7 verdicts; consolidated interview backlog; 8 MVP telemetry signals.

nodes.label: Finding: H1 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (travel is activation, safety plus home novelty is daily retention)
nodes.rationale: Travel route friction is frequent but the workaround economy mostly succeeds in 15 to 20 minutes; safety-aware routing and route novelty carry the strongest daily-pain evidence. Reframes the wedge story for Phase 4.

nodes.label: Unmet need: safety-aware routing (strongest evidence)
nodes.rationale: 54 percent of women runners changed routes over safety; 42 percent say safety dictates routine; Strava's generator has documented dangerous outputs; zero products accept safety as input.

nodes.label: Unmet need: route novelty and personalization at home
nodes.rationale: CityStrides (90k+ users, 6.7M streets) proves paying demand for roads-not-yet-run; incumbents rank by popularity, the opposite.

nodes.label: Interview backlog (validation plan for desk findings)
nodes.rationale: Priorities: committed amateurs (H1 base rate, bundling test, willingness to pay), women runners (algorithmic safety trust), frequent travelers (night-before ritual).

nodes.label: Open decision: must safety-critical routing be free (ethics and pricing)
nodes.rationale: Founder decision needed before Phase 6 pricing; flagged in personas and unmet-needs.

edges.rationale: The founding travel framing becomes the activation story; daily retention comes from safety and novelty.
The reframe is the key open input to the concept lock.
Pricing work cannot finalize the free tier boundary until this is decided.
MVP telemetry signals list defines what product data can replace interviews.
